# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Gao_2026_hydromorphone"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Gao_2026_hydromorphone"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70666> (open access, PMC13358379)
* Supplement (Figures S1-S5, Tables S1-S11): Supporting Information of the article

Gao 2026 describes hydromorphone given as a 72-hour weight-based continuous
infusion (0.03 mg/kg/h) to critically ill adults on extracorporeal membrane
oxygenation (ECMO). The distinguishing feature of the model is how it handles
the two ECMO modes. Rather than testing ECMO mode as a covariate on one or two
parameters, the authors estimate a **separate typical value of every
disposition parameter for veno-venous (V-V) and veno-arterial (V-A) ECMO**, in
one joint fit that shares a single set of inter-individual variability terms
across both modes. They justify this by noting that the two modes alter the
circulation differently, so a mode effect is likely to touch several
correlated parameters at once (Methods, "Structure Pharmacokinetic Model").

In the packaged model the mode is selected with the subject-level covariate
`ECMO_VA_STATUS` (1 = V-A, 0 = V-V). Every subject in the source cohort was on
ECMO, so `ECMO_VA_STATUS = 0` means V-V ECMO, not "no ECMO".

Model time is in **minutes** because the paper reports clearances in L/min;
the vignette converts to hours for plotting and NCA.

# Population

Gao 2026 enrolled 26 adults at the general ICU of Union Hospital, Wuhan,
between September 2022 and August 2024: 12 on V-V ECMO (all for respiratory
failure: viral pneumonia or ARDS, Pneumocystis pneumonia, post-traumatic ARDS,
fibrotic interstitial lung disease) and 14 on V-A ECMO (acute myocardial
infarction or viral myocarditis with cardiogenic shock) (Tables 1 and S2).
Ages were 25-77 years and body weights 45-102 kg; 9 of 26 patients were
female (11 of 12 V-V and 6 of 14 V-A patients were male). V-A patients had
markedly higher aminotransferases (median AST 195.5 vs 51 U/L, ALT 97 vs
39.5 U/L). Patients on continuous renal replacement therapy and patients
with Child-Pugh C liver disease were excluded. The analysis used 484 arterial
plasma concentrations (227 V-V, 257 V-A) drawn during the 72-hour infusion and
for 12 hours after it stopped.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Gao_2026_hydromorphone"))$population)
```

# Source trace

Every value below comes from Gao 2026 Table 2 ("Final model estimates").

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 3-compartment, first-order elimination from central | -- | Methods "Structure Pharmacokinetic Model"; Results; Table S3 (OFV 2323.90) |
| Mode-specific typical values, shared IIV | -- | Methods; Table 2 footnote (`CLVVi = exp(CLTVV + eta_i)`, `CLVAi = exp(CLTVA + eta_i)`) |
| `lcl_vv`, `lcl_va` | 0.955, 0.657 L/min | Table 2 CLVV, CLVA |
| `lvc_vv`, `lvc_va` | 23.6, 16.3 L | Table 2 V1VV, V1VA |
| `lq_vv`, `lq_va` (paper Q2) | 0.112, 0.075 L/min | Table 2 Q2VV, Q2VA |
| `lvp_vv`, `lvp_va` (paper V2) | 112, 72.8 L | Table 2 V2VV, V2VA |
| `lq2_vv`, `lq2_va` (paper Q3) | 1.48, 0.538 L/min | Table 2 Q3VV, Q3VA |
| `lvp2_vv`, `lvp2_va` (paper V3) | 87, 43 L | Table 2 V3VV, V3VA |
| `etalcl` variance | 0.276^2 | Table 2 IIV of CL 27.6 (approximate CV%) |
| `etalvc` variance | 0.572^2 | Table 2 IIV of V1 57.2 (approximate CV%) |
| `etalcl`-`etalvc` covariance | 0.0545 | Table 2 covariance between CL and V1 |
| `etalq` variance | 1.40^2 | Table 2 IIV of Q2 140 (approximate CV%) |
| `propSd` | 0.185 | Table 2 proportional error 18.5% |
| `addSd` | 1.7 ng/mL | Table 2 additive error |
| Residual model `Cc ~ add + prop` | -- | Methods: `C(t)ij = C_hat(t)ij x (1 + eps_prop,ij) + eps_add,ij` |
| Dose | 0.03 mg/kg/h for 72 h | Methods "Dosing of Hydromorphone" |

# Virtual cohort

The cohort reproduces the 26 study patients from Table S2 (ECMO mode and body
weight, which sets the weight-based infusion rate), each replicated 8 times
to give 96 V-V and 112 V-A virtual subjects.

```{r cohort}
table_s2 <- data.frame(
  patient = 1:26,
  mode = c(
    "V-A", "V-A", "V-V", "V-V", "V-V", "V-A", "V-A", "V-V", "V-V", "V-V",
    "V-V", "V-V", "V-V", "V-V", "V-V", "V-V", "V-A", "V-A", "V-A", "V-A",
    "V-A", "V-A", "V-A", "V-A", "V-A", "V-A"
  ),
  WT = c(
    70, 70, 70, 80, 60, 70, 62, 78, 102, 99, 78, 60, 70, 65, 75, 65,
    45, 54, 80, 68, 70, 56, 50, 52, 75, 55
  )
)
# Medians match the Table S5 footnote (72.5 kg V-V, 65 kg V-A).
table_s2 |>
  group_by(mode) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median_WT = median(WT), .groups = "drop")

n_rep <- 8L
cohort <- table_s2[rep(seq_len(nrow(table_s2)), each = n_rep), ] |>
  mutate(
    id = seq_len(n()),
    ECMO_VA_STATUS = as.integer(mode == "V-A")
  )
```

# Simulation

Each subject receives 0.03 mg/kg/h for 72 h (4320 min) into `central` and is
observed on `central` every 15 min to 96 h, with a denser grid around the end
of the infusion.

```{r events}
infusion_min <- 72 * 60
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 96 * 60, by = 15),
  infusion_min + c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40)
)))

dose_rows <- cohort |>
  transmute(
    id, time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
    rate = 0.03 * WT / 60, # mg/min
    amt = 0.03 * WT * 72, # mg over 72 h
    ECMO_VA_STATUS, WT, mode
  )
obs_rows <- cohort |>
  select(id, ECMO_VA_STATUS, WT, mode) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", rate = 0, amt = 0)
events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
```

```{r simulate}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Gao_2026_hydromorphone"))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261025)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("mode", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(time_h = time / 60)
```

## Individual profiles (Figure 3)

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Gao 2026: individual hydromorphone profiles for the 26 study patients (one simulated replicate each; prediction without residual error)."}
sim |>
  filter(id %in% cohort$id[seq(1, nrow(cohort), by = n_rep)]) |>
  ggplot(aes(time_h, Cc, group = id, colour = mode, linetype = mode)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("V-V" = "steelblue", "V-A" = "red")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 96, 24)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (hour)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = NULL, linetype = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper's Figure 3 shows plateaus of roughly 25-70 ng/mL for V-V and
30-80 ng/mL for V-A, with V-A sitting higher; the simulation reproduces both
the range and the ordering.

## Prediction interval by mode (Figure 2)

```{r fig2, fig.cap = "Simulated median and 95% prediction interval (with residual error) by ECMO mode; compare with the pcVPC in Figure 2 of Gao 2026."}
sim |>
  group_by(mode, time_h) |>
  summarise(
    p025 = quantile(sim, 0.025), p50 = median(sim), p975 = quantile(sim, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time_h)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p025, ymax = p975), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  facet_wrap(~mode) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 96, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time (hour)", y = "Hydromorphone (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

Gao 2026 summarises exposure as the area under the curve from 0 to 96 h
(AUC0-96h) and the concentration at the end of the 72-h infusion (C72h),
computed from each patient's individual (post hoc) profile (Tables S5-S11).
Because the profiles rise monotonically during the infusion (Figure 3),
C72h equals Cmax over 0-72 h, so both metrics are PKNCA interval
parameters. The input is the model prediction `Cc` without residual error,
matching the paper's post hoc profiles.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, mode, time_h, Cc)
dose <- cohort |>
  transmute(id, mode, time_h = 0, amt = 0.03 * WT * 72)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time_h | mode + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time_h | mode + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0), end = c(96, 72),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE), cmax = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_gm <- as.data.frame(nca) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax")) |>
  group_by(mode, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = exp(mean(log(PPORRES))), .groups = "drop")
nca_gm
```

## Comparison with the published exposures

The paper does not tabulate an overall geometric mean, but Tables S5-S11 split
each mode into two equal halves (6 + 6 V-V, 7 + 7 V-A) and give each half's
geometric mean, so the overall geometric mean is the square root of the
product of the two halves. Table S5 (body-weight split) is used here; the other
splits give the same overall value to within rounding.

```{r compare}
reference <- data.frame(
  mode = c("V-V", "V-A"),
  auclast = c(sqrt(2650 * 2900), sqrt(3150 * 3600)),
  cmax = c(sqrt(37.1 * 40.3), sqrt(43.9 * 50.1))
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = tidyr::pivot_wider(nca_gm, names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES),
  reference = reference,
  by = "mode",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL", cmax = "ng/mL")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Geometric-mean AUC0-96h (Table S5) and C72h (shown as Cmax over 0-72 h), simulated vs Gao 2026.")
```

```{r compare-assert}
pct_diff <- with(
  dplyr::inner_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(reference, -mode, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    nca_gm,
    by = c("mode", "PPTESTCD")
  ),
  100 * (PPORRES - ref) / ref
)
pct_diff
# A mis-transcribed clearance or volume, or a minute/hour slip in the
# infusion rate, moves these geometric means by tens of percent; the
# Monte-Carlo error of a ~100-subject geometric mean at 28% CV is about 3%.
stopifnot(all(abs(pct_diff) < 15))
```

The V-A / V-V exposure ratio is the paper's headline finding (V-A patients may
need less hydromorphone):

```{r ratio}
nca_gm |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(ratio_VA_to_VV = `V-A` / `V-V`)
```

# Closed-form check: steady state

For a linear model under a constant infusion, the steady-state concentration
is the infusion rate divided by clearance, independent of the distribution
parameters. Solving the typical-value model (no IIV) for long enough to
reach steady state checks the ODE system and the mg/L to ng/mL conversion.

```{r steady-state}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ_pars <- data.frame(
  mode = c("V-V", "V-A"),
  cl = c(0.955, 0.657), vc = c(23.6, 16.3), q = c(0.112, 0.075),
  vp = c(112, 72.8), q2 = c(1.48, 0.538), vp2 = c(87, 43)
)
# Slowest eigenvalue of the 3-compartment rate matrix -> terminal half-life.
terminal_half_life_min <- function(p) {
  k <- matrix(c(
    -(p$cl + p$q + p$q2) / p$vc, p$q / p$vp, p$q2 / p$vp2,
    p$q / p$vc, -p$q / p$vp, 0,
    p$q2 / p$vc, 0, -p$q2 / p$vp2
  ), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  log(2) / min(abs(Re(eigen(k)$values)))
}
typ_pars$t_half_h <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(typ_pars)), function(i) {
  terminal_half_life_min(typ_pars[i, ]) / 60
})
typ_pars

rate_mg_min <- 0.03 * 70 / 60
t_end <- ceiling(15 * max(typ_pars$t_half_h)) * 60
# One single-subject solve per mode: the typical-value model has no omega.
ss_conc <- sapply(c(0L, 1L), function(va) {
  ss_events <- data.frame(
    id = 1L,
    time = c(0, t_end),
    evid = c(1L, 0L),
    cmt = "central",
    amt = c(rate_mg_min * t_end, 0),
    rate = c(rate_mg_min, 0),
    ECMO_VA_STATUS = va
  )
  ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ss_events, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10) |>
    as.data.frame()
  ss$Cc[ss$time == t_end]
})
ss_check <- data.frame(
  mode = c("V-V", "V-A"),
  simulated = ss_conc,
  closed_form = 1000 * rate_mg_min / typ_pars$cl
) |>
  mutate(rel_err = abs(simulated - closed_form) / closed_form)
ss_check
stopifnot(all(ss_check$rel_err < 1e-4))
```

At 70 kg the typical steady-state concentrations are 36.6 ng/mL (V-V) and
53.3 ng/mL (V-A). The paper's geometric-mean C72h values are about 39 and
47 ng/mL. The V-A value is lower than its 70 kg steady state because the V-A
patients were lighter (median 65 kg) and so received a lower absolute infusion
rate, and because 72 h is about 5.5 terminal half-lives (about 13 h in both
modes), so the slow peripheral compartment has not quite filled.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Inter-individual variability scale.** Table 2 reports the IIV of CL, V1
  and Q2 as "approximate CV%", the first-order approximation
  CV = 100 x sqrt(omega^2), so the variances are entered as (CV/100)^2:
  0.0762, 0.327 and 1.96. The CL-V1 covariance (0.0545) is printed on the
  variance scale and gives a correlation of 0.345. Reading the CVs instead
  as exact log-normal CVs (omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)) would give 0.0734, 0.283
  and 1.085; the difference matters only for the large Q2 term.
* **Residual error.** The proportional error "18.5%" and the additive error
  1.7 ng/mL are taken as standard deviations of two independent epsilons,
  as written in the paper's residual equation; the pooled-model Table S4
  labels the same quantities "SD".
* **Compartment numbering.** The paper's Q2/V2 (peripheral compartment 1,
  the slow one) maps to `q`/`vp` and Q3/V3 (peripheral compartment 2) to
  `q2`/`vp2`. Only Q2 carries IIV; the paper estimated no IIV on V2, Q3 or
  V3.
* **Time unit.** Clearances are in L/min as published, so the model runs in
  minutes; infusion rates and observation times above are in minutes.
* **Exposure references.** The published AUC0-96h and C72h are geometric means
  of individual post hoc profiles of the 26 patients; the comparison uses a
  simulated cohort of the same patients (mode and weight from Table S2)
  with IIV drawn from the model, so the two agree in expectation but not
  patient by patient.
* **Not reproduced.** The exploratory comparisons of exposure by albumin,
  ALT, AST, bilirubin, creatinine clearance, lactate, age and weight
  (Tables S5-S11) split the post hoc profiles by observed covariates that are
  not in the model, so they cannot be reproduced by simulation. The pooled
  sensitivity model with ECMO mode on V2 only (Table S4) is not the final
  model and is not packaged. The post-/pre-oxygenator concentration ratio
  (Figure 4) was close to 1 throughout, so the model has no circuit
  sequestration term.
* **ECMO mode covariate.** `ECMO_VA_STATUS` is the V-A member of a mode
  indicator; the source's own mode column is coded 1 = V-V, 2 = V-A
  (Figure S5 caption), so `ECMO_VA_STATUS = MODE - 1`.
